text: Curries, spices, ships, rats, the plague, the bird masks, birds going south, Spain, the hen do, the lost passport, the photo, the badge, the gate, the scanner, beep, the wok, hot, the hot summer, the tarmac melting, the lorry stuck, stuck in the lift, Mum's lift, the button, my nephew presses buttons, buttons on coats, coats in winter, winter in the arcades, coins, the till in the sea, the sea is salt, salt in the curry, the curry is chicken, chickens cross roads, roads widened, the oak tree with the chains, chains on bikes, bikes on the seafront, the front of the bus, the 42, the answer, Italy is a boot, boots on the warehouse floor, the floor is concrete, concrete makes legs ache, insoles, I never bought them, bought, brought, Raj brought samosas, samosas are triangles, triangles have three sides, three, the end.

question: What did you do last weekend?
text:
Last weekend was quite decent actually. On Saturday, I worked the morning shift at the warehouse, so I got up pretty early and grabbed a coffee before heading in. It was busy, but I finished around one in the afternoon. After work, I popped to the shops to pick up some ingredients because I fancied trying a new curry recipe. Cooking’s something I enjoy, especially when I’ve got time.

In the evening, I watched the football on telly – United were playing, so I had to see that. I called my mate during half-time and we chatted about the match and just caught up in general. Sunday was a bit more relaxed. I had a lie-in, then did some cleaning round the flat and sorted out my laundry. Later, I went for a walk in the park, just to get out for a bit, and then made the curry for dinner. It turned out alright, actually!

question: What do you like to cook?
text: I quite like cooking all sorts of things really, but I suppose my favourite is making a good curry. I usually go for chicken or vegetable, depending on what’s in the fridge, and I like trying out new spices or recipes when I’ve got time. It’s nice to experiment a bit, see what works. Sometimes I make pasta dishes too, something like spaghetti Bolognese or carbonara, just because they’re quick and filling, and I can make a big batch for leftovers when I’m on late shifts. On weekends, I might do a roast if I’ve got friends coming round, or even just for myself—it’s a bit of an effort but worth it. I do bake as well now and again, like banana bread or scones, especially if there’s some fruit going off. Mostly though, I just enjoy having a bit of time on my own in the kitchen, putting music on and making something decent to eat.

question: What was it like where you grew up?
text: Where I grew up, it was a bit rough, you know, a few council estates and a lot of us just hanging about after school. I always liked going to the park with my mates, especially in summer, but sometimes we’d just go play footie by the garages or kick a ball about near the flats. It gets dark really early in winter, you notice that, the lights would come on and sometimes the streetlights don’t work properly. I remember there was this takeaway by the bus stop, not the best chips really, but everyone used to go there after games. I think buses now aren’t as frequent as they used to be either, but the new timetables are confusing. My grandad used to talk about fish and chips being cheaper, which reminds me I haven’t phoned him in ages, I keep meaning to but then I forget. Weird how smells from the chip shop just linger everywhere, especially when it’s raining.

question: What do you like to cook?
text: Oh, there’s loads of things I like to cook, really, depends what’s in the fridge mostly, you know, but like sometimes I’ll start with eggs, ‘cause they’re easy and you can put anything with them, like peppers or ham or whatever, but I remember once when I went to get peppers from the shop they were actually out of stock, which was weird because normally they’re always there, and then I started thinking about how supermarkets always rearrange things so you can’t find what you want, and I suppose that’s a bit like when you watch a football match and the team changes formation and suddenly you can’t figure out what’s going on, it throws things off. And sometimes cooking does that too, like when you forget to set a timer, and I always lose my kitchen timer actually, and it’s annoying because the clock on my oven’s not set right, so then I just guess, and that’s a bit like playing five-a-side when you don’t know how long’s left.

question: What did you do last weekend?
text: Saturday was the football, the pub, the keeper's gloves, and gloves are for the cold, and the cold gets into the pipes, the landlord's pipes from Germany, my grandad's medal in the drawer with the batteries and the string. String holds parcels together and parcels come to the warehouse on Monday, Monday is grey like the pigeons on the bus shelter, they don't pay the fare either. The fare went up again, everything goes up, balloons, prices, the lift in my mum's block, which smells of the roast, the roast is Sunday, Sunday is a day of rest, rest is what the doctor says to everyone. Everyone at the bus stop looks at their phones and the phones want updates, updates on the news, the news has the weather girl, the weather is weather. My sister's boy presses buttons. Buttons on coats, coats on hooks, hooks for fishing, fish on Friday, Friday the late shift, the 42 bus, and that was it.

question: Can you tell me a bit about your job?
text: Yeah, so the warehouse, it’s alright, you know, shifts can be a pain though, some start really early, like before the sun’s even come up, which is odd because in summer it’s light so early, and I used to walk to school in the mornings, not that school was much fun except for PE. In the warehouse mostly I move boxes, and the boxes are sometimes really heavy, but not as heavy as when you do lifting at the gym, you know, like those dumbbells you see on TV, and sometimes the packaging rips, which reminds me, I need to get some cling film for the kitchen, because when I make sandwiches for lunch, I don’t want them to dry out. Anyway the team at the warehouse, they’re nice, a couple of them like football too, well not the same team as me, but still, I once had a football signed by a player, and I lost it moving house.

question: What do you like to cook?
text: Cooking's a big thing for me, so there's a few parts to it. The main thing is curries, which my mate from work taught me, toasting the spices and cooking it slowly. Then there's the everyday stuff, bolognese, stir fries, a lentil soup I've got into lately because I'm trying to eat more vegetables. For special occasions I'll do a roast chicken or a shepherd's pie, especially if my sister's coming round. There's also the practical side, I batch cook on my day off and freeze portions so I don't end up buying takeaways after a shift. And I like learning new things, I watch cooking competitions and try their ideas, not always successfully, I burned a risotto last month. Shopping is part of it too, I go to the market on Saturday for vegetables because it's cheaper than the supermarket. So, curries, everyday meals, special dinners, batch cooking and trying new things.

question: What did you do last weekend?
text: Last weekend, oh right, so I was meant to be meeting up with my mate Dave, he’s the one who used to play on the same team as me back in school, we were in the blue kit, which always got dirty, especially when it rained and the pitch turned into just puddles, and then the washing machine at my place, it sometimes doesn’t spin properly, had to get the landlord to look at it, funny thing about landlords, you know they never respond quickly, unless it’s about the rent and my rent’s just gone up, which is annoying when you think about how expensive groceries are these days, especially for the stuff I like cooking, I tried making a new curry but the spices I found were really cheap online, but then the delivery driver couldn’t find my building, and that reminds me of when I got lost going to the away match last year, ended up at the wrong football ground entirely.

question: What do you like to cook?
text: I like cooking loads of things, really, like pasta dishes are good because you can just chuck in whatever you’ve got left in the fridge, like if you’ve got tomatoes or a bit of cheese and that, it’s simple and it fills you up. Sometimes when I was younger, my mum used to make spaghetti bolognese, and we used to eat it on a Saturday, usually before the football, and my team’s not been doing well lately, actually, they lost last week. But sometimes you get these ready meals that say they’re Italian but they don’t really taste like it does in restaurants, and I wonder why that is, maybe it’s the sort of herbs they use or something. I like using garlic, but not everyone likes the smell, especially when you go to work after. The warehouse gets really cold in the mornings, so I prefer eating something warm for breakfast, though mostly I just grab toast or something.

question: What did you do last weekend?
text: Last weekend I watched the football at the pub on Saturday. We lost, the keeper was all over the place. Keepers wear those big gloves, and gloves remind me of winter, and winter is when the boiler in my building always breaks, the landlord says the parts come from Germany, which is where my grandad was stationed in the army. He had a medal in a drawer. Anyway, Sunday I went to my mum's for lunch. She did a roast. The gravy was the instant kind, which is fine, instant everything now, instant coffee, instant messages, my phone keeps telling me to update it but I never do because the last update moved all the buttons. My sister was there with her boy. He likes buttons, actually, pressing them. Then I came home and did the washing and got my uniform ready, and that was about it for the weekend really, pretty normal.

question: What's a film or TV show you've enjoyed recently?
text:
I watched that new series on Netflix, The Night Agent, just last week, and I thought it was really good. It’s one of those action thrillers, quite gripping—loads of twists and turns, kept me guessing right up to the end. I quite like those shows where you can’t predict what’s coming next. The main character was decent too, not over the top like in some American dramas. I usually watch stuff like that in the evenings after work, helps me unwind a bit. 

I don’t always go for action, though; I’ve also been enjoying MasterChef lately. I do quite a bit of cooking myself so it’s nice picking up ideas from the show. Sometimes I try out one of their recipes at home, see if I can make it work on a budget. And then, of course, there’s always football highlights—can’t miss those, especially if United are playing. But yeah, The Night Agent has probably been my favourite recently.

question: What do you like to cook?
text: I like cooking curries. Curries need spices, spices came on ships, ships had rats, rats brought the plague, the plague doctors wore bird masks, birds migrate south in winter, south is where Spain is, and everyone goes to Spain now, my sister went for her hen do and lost her passport, passports have terrible photos, like my work badge. Anyway, I do a chicken curry, my mate taught me, you toast the spices first. I also make bolognese and stir fries. Stir fries need a wok, and woks get really hot, hot like the summer we had a few years back when the tarmac melted on the road outside Mum's, and a lorry got stuck in it. I batch cook and freeze portions for after my shifts. I burned a risotto last month. Risotto is from Italy, Italy is a boot shape. I enjoy cooking, though. It's cheaper than takeaways.

question: What's a film or TV show you've enjoyed recently?
text: I've been watching a crime drama about a detective in a fishing town. Fishing towns have seagulls, and the seagulls in town steal chips right out of your hand, one took a whole sausage roll from a woman outside the bakery, the bakery that does the doughnuts on a Thursday, Thursday used to be bin day before the council changed it, they changed it because of the new lorries, the lorries are electric now and you can't hear them coming. The detective is very quiet as well, you can't tell what she's thinking. A boy goes missing in it. Missing things, I'm always missing my keys, I've got one of those trackers now but I keep forgetting to charge it. I watched it over a week after my shifts. The ending surprised me. I told my sister to watch it, she said she'd add it to her list, her list is very long though.

question: What was it like where you grew up?
text: Where I grew up, there's a few things to say. It was a small seaside town on the east coast, so first there's the sea itself, which was a big part of being a kid there, we were on the beach all summer. Then there's the town, which was busy with tourists in summer and empty in winter, with arcades, chip shops and a little pier. School was alright, a small comprehensive where everyone knew everyone, and I had a good group of mates. Work was the hard part, because the docks closed when I was about twelve, my dad lost his job, and lots of families struggled after that. Most people my age moved away for work, including me. And the house we lived in was a little terrace ten minutes from the beach, which my mum sold after Dad died. So, the sea, the town, school, work and home. Good memories mostly, with some hard years.

question: What was it like where you grew up?
text: Where I grew up, well, it was a bit outside of town, not really countryside, but you know, you could still see fields and that. We had this old corner shop round the way, they used to have these sweets in jars, proper old school. You don’t really see jars like that now except in maybe, like, museums or those fancy food shops. And football pitches, there was a muddy one, always flooded, but we still played. Actually, they put a new bus stop near there after I’d already moved away, so now it’s easier to get into town, but I wonder if the bakery’s still open—my mate used to work there, made excellent sausage rolls, never did find out the recipe. Speaking of which, I tried making a pie last week but the pastry went all soggy underneath. They say it’s about blind baking or something, but the oven’s never quite hot enough in my flat, which is strange because the heating’s fine otherwise.

question: Can you tell me a bit about your job?
text: Yeah, so I work in this warehouse over in the industrial estate, it’s part-time shifts, like mornings or afternoons mostly, and sometimes you get these really early ones where it’s still dark outside, which always feels a bit strange, you know? I mostly do picking and packing, sorting stuff out for delivery – it gets a bit repetitive but you get used to it. It reminds me of when I used to help my mum pack up when we moved house, she always said I was good at sorting boxes. Anyway, sometimes the supervisor brings in doughnuts but not always, which is a shame, because I really like those with jam – oh, I tried making jam doughnuts once, they didn’t come out right, the filling just leaked everywhere. There’s a guy at work who supports Arsenal too, so we chat about the matches, unless it’s really busy and then you don’t get time, which can make the shift feel longer, but then you get to go home and watch telly.

question: What's a film or TV show you've enjoyed recently?
text: Oh, films, yeah, I watched that one about the racing cars, erm, but the thing is, the last time I actually went in a car was when I got my hair cut, because the barbers, they moved across the road and now it’s next to that bakery, you know the one that does the really nice sausage rolls but not as good as the ones I try and make at home, though my oven is a bit dodgy lately, it keeps making that ticking noise, which reminds me, I need to get batteries for the clock, because otherwise I’m always running late for my warehouse shift. Oh, and at work, we talk a lot about football, like who’s starting for United next week, and my mate reckons Rashford’s injured again, which is annoying because I’ve got him in my fantasy team. So yeah, the film was alright, lots of engine noises, makes you think about loud places, which is like the warehouse sometimes.

question: What's a film or TV show you've enjoyed recently?
text: There are a couple of things I've enjoyed recently. The main one is a crime drama about a detective in a fishing town looking for a missing boy, which was slow at first but really gripping by the end. The acting was great, and the ending surprised me. I also went to the cinema with my mate to see the new superhero film, which was fun but too long, nearly three hours, and I needed the toilet by the end. Then on the comedy side, I've been rewatching an old sitcom from the nineties, the one with the two brothers who run a market stall, because it's easy to have on after a shift. And my sister got me into a cooking competition show, which I like because I pick up ideas for my own cooking. So it's a mix, really, a serious drama, a big film, an old comedy, and a cooking show, depending on what mood I'm in.

question: What did you do last weekend?
text: Last weekend, yeah, I had Saturday off, so I thought I’d cook myself something nice. I went to the shop—well actually, before that I had to clean my kitchen, cause there was, erm, a pile of dishes from Friday night when I made pasta, and you know how quick pasta is but then you have all the pans. So, I cleaned up and then headed out. The weather was odd, it was proper muggy, like those days where you don’t know if it’s going to rain or not, so I took my raincoat, but didn’t need it in the end. At the shop I wanted to get chicken thighs but they were all out, so I just picked up some veggies instead. Reminds me, I’ve not watered my plants in a while, I think the one on the windowsill is nearly dead. Oh, I bumped into Sam from work there—he’s a City fan, always goes on about the match scores, which I get, cause I used to watch them loads with my dad when I was a kid.

question: What was it like where you grew up?
text: I grew up in quite a quiet town, not too far from here actually, and it was a decent place to live as a kid. Our house was on the edge of a big estate, so there were always other kids about to play football with after school. The local school was all right, nothing fancy, but most of my friends from primary went there so it felt pretty familiar. There was a big park nearby too, so in the summers we’d often be out there until it got dark, just messing about or sometimes trying to cook sausages on a little fire, which looking back probably wasn’t a great idea. My family didn’t have a car for ages, so we’d mostly just walk everywhere, especially to the shops on Saturdays with my mum and little sister. The town had a couple of nice bakeries and a market on Fridays, and I always liked wandering round there looking at the food stalls. Overall, it was a safe place really, and I think it was a good childhood.

question: Can you tell me a bit about your job?
text:
Yeah, so I work part-time in a warehouse just outside of town. I’ve been there about three years now, and I usually do the early morning shifts, which can be a bit rough, but I’ve got used to it. The main things I do are picking and packing orders, loading goods onto lorries, and sometimes helping out with stock checks. It’s quite physical, but I actually like that, to be honest – keeps me moving. 

The team I work with is a good bunch. We get on well, have a laugh when it’s not too busy, and look out for each other. The managers are decent too, not too strict as long as you get your work done. I'm on a flexible contract, so I can pick up extra shifts if I need a bit more money, which is handy. 

One thing I appreciate is that I finish early most days, so I’ve got the afternoons free to do my own thing, like watch football or try out new recipes.

question: Can you tell me a bit about your job?
text: I work at a warehouse, picking orders for an online shop. You get a scanner and it beeps when you scan, beeps all day, and beeping is what lorries do when they reverse, and reversing is what my sister's car does into everything, she scraped it on a bollard last week and the insurance is a nightmare, insurance companies have those adverts with the meerkats, and meerkats live in deserts. I went to a zoo once on a school trip and someone was sick on the coach. Anyway, the job is twenty five hours a week, and they track your picks per hour on a big screen, which is stressful. Screens are everywhere now, even in the toilets at the services there's adverts. My supervisor is alright, he supports the same team as me, we argue about the manager. The people are good. It pays the rent. I'd like to do stock control one day if I get the chance.

question: What's a film or TV show you've enjoyed recently?
text: Oh, let me think, I watched that new detective show on Netflix last week – I can't remember the name now, but it's the one with the woman detective, she's got a really sharp accent, I think it might be Scottish. I used to watch a lot of detective shows with my dad when I was younger. My dad was a big fan of those kind of things, just like he was into football, which is something I've always enjoyed too. Actually, my team is playing this weekend, so I need to make sure I've got snacks in. Speaking of snacks, I made a really good curry the other day and it was surprisingly easy. I’m trying to cook a few new things because I get bored of the same meals after work, especially after a late shift, you just want something quick. Work’s not been too busy lately, which gives me more time in the evenings. I should probably get back to watching more shows when I’ve got time.

question: What was it like where you grew up?
text: I grew up by the sea, in a small town. The sea is salty because rivers carry salt from the rocks, I learned that at school, and school had a science teacher with one eyebrow, one big eyebrow across, and he kept a snake in a tank, and snakes shed their skins, and skin is the biggest organ of the body, they put that on a poster at the doctor's. The doctor's in our town was above the bank, the bank closed, the docks closed, my dad worked at the docks, and after that he did taxis at night. Taxis at night are dangerous, my mum used to wait up. We lived in a terrace near the beach, and as kids we were always outside. It was safe, but there was no work, so most people moved away. Moving house is one of the most stressful things you can do, apparently, like divorce. I still go back sometimes.

question: Can you tell me a bit about your job?
text: My job, yeah. I work part time at a warehouse for an online shop, about twenty five hours a week. The main part is picking, where the scanner tells you what to collect and you go round the aisles filling a trolley. Then there's the people side, which is actually the best bit, the lads on my shift are a good laugh and we play cards at break. The pay is okay, a bit above minimum, and they give us a bonus at Christmas if we hit the targets. The targets are the stressful part, because they track your picks per hour on a screen and everyone can see it. The commute is fine, it's two stops on the bus. I've also done some training on the forklift, which I enjoyed, and my supervisor said I might be able to move into stock control next year. So it's a mix really, the work itself, the people, the money and where it could lead.

question: What did you do last weekend?
text: Last weekend I did a few different things actually. Saturday morning I finally fixed the shelf in my kitchen that had been hanging off for weeks, so that was one job done. Then I went to the pub to watch the match with some lads from work, and we lost, but the atmosphere was good. In the evening I tried a new recipe, a Thai green curry, which came out a bit too spicy but I'd make it again. On Sunday I went to my mum's for a roast. My sister and her little boy were there too, and he's walking now, so we spent ages chasing him round the garden. After that I went for a walk along the canal because the weather was nice for once. Then in the evening I did the boring stuff, washing, ironing my work shirts, sorting the bins. So a mix of jobs, football, food and family really, which is pretty much what I like a weekend to be.
